studies.Reference: Vitamin d pathway genes, diet, and risk of renal cell carcinoma.
studies.Title: Vitamin d pathway genes, diet, and risk of renal cell carcinoma.
studies.Authors: Karami S, Brennan P, Navratilova M, Mates D, Zaridze D, Janout V, Kollarova H, Bencko V, Matveev V, Szesznia-Dabrowska N, Holcatova I, Yeager M, Chanock S, Rothman N, Boffetta P, Chow WH, Moore LE
studies.Population: Hospital-based RCC cases and controls from seven centers in four Central and Eastern European countries

sample_size.excerpt: Suitable quantity and quality of genomic DNA was obtained from a subset of 777 (70.8%) eligible RCC cases and 1035 (70.1%) controls enrolled in our study.
sample_size.location: Section 2.1 Study Population, paragraph 1; total_n derived from reported group counts 777 + 1035 = 1812

cases.excerpt: A total of 1097 incident, histologically confirmed RCC cases and 1476 controls were included in this study. Suitable quantity and quality of genomic DNA was obtained from a subset of 777 (70.8%) eligible RCC cases and 1035 (70.1%) controls enrolled in our study.

p_value.excerpt: In contrast, increased RCC risk was observed with increasing consumption frequency of yogurt ( P -trend = .04).

comparison.excerpt: All dietary intake frequencies in this study were assessed in tertiles based on the frequency of dietary intake among controls.

design.excerpt: Briefly, from 1999 through 2003, a hospital-based case-control study of RCC was conducted in seven centers in four countries of Central and Eastern Europe

timing.excerpt: from 1999 through 2003, a hospital-based case-control study of RCC was conducted in seven centers in four countries of Central and Eastern Europe

continent.excerpt: from 1999 through 2003, a hospital-based case-control study of RCC was conducted in seven centers in four countries of Central and Eastern Europe

ethnicity.excerpt: conducted in seven centers in four countries of Central and Eastern Europe (Moscow, Russia; Bucharest, Romania; Lodz, Poland; Prague, Olomouc, Ceske-Budejovice, and Brno, Czech Republic).

exposure_measurement.excerpt: A food frequency questionnaire was comprised of 23 food items, which the study investigators selected by consensus during the planning stage of the study and further validated during the pilot stage
